title: Existence of prefix deletion equivalence
statement: Let I be a linearly ordered type, p≥0, n=p+2 and t:Fin(n)→I. Use cechStableSort and cechPartialSort [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. Let O consist of (σ,a,τ,r) with σ,τ permutations of Fin(n), a:Fin(n), r:Fin(n+1), σ stable for t, τ partial sorted with prefix a, and r<a. Let N consist of (j,ρ,b,η) with j:Fin(n), ρ,η permutations of Fin(n-1), b:Fin(n-1), ρ stable for t∘j.succAbove, η partial sorted with prefix b, and (t(j),j) strictly preceding (t(j.succAbove(ρ(b))),j.succAbove(ρ(b))) lexicographically. There exists e:O≃N such that for e(σ,a,τ,r)=(j,ρ,b,η), a=b+1, r<n and τ(r)=j. This statement does not assert the two permutation restriction identities.

proof.text: Construct deletePerm by restricting a permutation to complementary subtypes and conjugating by complement equivalences. The private restriction identity is generalized to an arbitrary source-complement enumeration; increasing enumeration is its specialization here. Prove stable sorting is preserved by any square of strictly increasing position and label embeddings, then specialize to succAbove. The lexicographic comparison criterion is proved for arbitrary linearly ordered position and label types with a monotone key and increasing ties. When r<a and a=b+1, the restricted permutations retain prefix agreement and an increasing tail. At b the restricted stable permutation has the old entry at a, so the comparison criterion gives the incoming before condition. This defines prefix_delete with the required prefix-length and omitted-label facts.

Prove prefix_delete injective: apply Mathlib Tuple.eq_sort_iff directly to identify the stable permutations; the prefix-length identity recovers a; apply ExistsUnique.unique directly to cechPartialSort_existsUnique to recover the other permutation; its injectivity and the omitted-label identity recover r.

For an incoming tuple (j,rho,b,eta), construct sigma=Tuple.sort t and set r=sigma.symm j. The increasing-restriction lemma and Tuple.eq_sort_iff identify its deletion with rho. The before condition and the general comparison criterion imply r<=b. Set a=b+1 and obtain the unique partial sort tau of sigma at a. Prefix deletion preserves partial sorting; apply ExistsUnique.unique directly to cechPartialSort_existsUnique to identify the deletion of tau with eta. The outgoing tuple (sigma,a,tau,r) therefore maps to the prescribed incoming tuple. Equiv.ofBijective completes the construction, and prefix_delete_spec supplies its two required facts.

theorem prefixDeletionExistence {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : ({x : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 2) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 3) //
    (cechStableSort t x.1 ∧ cechPartialSort x.1 x.2.2.1 x.2.1) ∧
      x.2.2.2.val < x.2.1.val}) ≃
      ({y : Fin (p + 2) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) × Fin (p + 1) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) //
    (cechStableSort (t ∘ y.1.succAbove) y.2.1 ∧
      cechPartialSort y.2.1 y.2.2.2 y.2.2.1) ∧
    (t y.1 < t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∨
      (t y.1 = t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∧
        y.1 < y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)))}), ∀ x,
      let y := e x
      x.1.2.1.val = y.1.2.2.1.val + 1 ∧
      ∃ hr : x.1.2.2.2.val < p + 2,
        x.1.2.2.1 ⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ = y.1.1
